title: Structure, Magnetic Property, Bacteriostatic Activity, and Large Magnetocaloric Effect of a Tetranuclear Gd(III)-Based Cluster

synthesis.procedure: Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.15 mmol, 0.0677 g), H6L (0.15 mmol, 0.0424 g), and acetic acid (45 μL) were dissolved in a mixed solvent of CH3OH (5.0 mL), CH3CN (5.0 mL), and CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL). The mixture was sealed in a 20 mL glass sample vase and heated at 80 °C for 18 h under autogenous pressure to yield yellow block-shaped crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solvothermal synthesis in a sealed 20 mL glass sample vase under autogenous pressure
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: yellow block-shaped crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction formed in the reaction mixture

properties.summary: Cluster 1 shows weak antiferromagnetic coupling among the butterfly Gd4 core and a large cryogenic magnetocaloric effect, making it a candidate molecular magnetic refrigerant. Room-temperature χMT matches four free Gd(III) ions; χMT then falls at low T, Curie–Weiss θ is small and negative, and fitted J1/J2 are weakly antiferromagnetic. Magnetization at 2.0 K approaches the 28 Nβ saturation value, and −ΔSm reaches 40.6 J·kg−1·K−1 at 2.0 K and ΔH = 7.0 T, slightly below the 43.1 J·kg−1·K−1 theoretical limit for four uncoupled Gd(III) ions.
